subject: Banking
title: Why Banks Keep Failing
description: A 60-second lesson on Why Banks Keep Failing.

hook.text: Banks have failed for 4,000 years. The causes repeat: excess leverage, risky bets, fraud, and loss of public confidence.

buildup.text: Every banking crisis follows a pattern: innovation, euphoria, over-lending, then collapse. The cycle never breaks.

discovery.text: Humans are wired for short-term thinking. Bankers optimize for this quarter's profit, not the next decade's stability.

twist.text: Regulations written after each crisis get weakened during the next boom. Memory fades, rules relax, and risk returns.

climax.text: Banking failures are systemic, not accidental. The incentive structure rewards risk-taking until the system breaks.

punchline.text: Same causes for 4,000 years. Leverage, risk, fraud, and lost trust.

quiz.question: Why do banking crises keep repeating?
options: Structural incentives reward risk-taking, and regulations weaken over time
